title: Bias–Variance
motto: Every model error comes from one of three sources: bias, variance, or noise. You can only control the first two.

steps.title: Core idea
steps.body: Every model error comes from one of three sources: bias, variance, or noise. You can only control the first two.

steps.title: Why this matters
cards: You trained a model. It has some error on test data. Where does that error come from?

If your model is too simple (linear regression on a curved dataset), it will consistently miss the true pattern. That is bias. If your model is too complex (degree-20 polynomial on 15 data points), it will fit the training data perfectly but give wildly different predictions on new data. That is variance.

steps.title: The concept
steps.body: High bias = underfitting. High variance = overfitting. MSE decomposes into bias² + variance + noise.
